## Biological Interpretation

The metabolomics analysis reveals a pronounced perturbation of **xenobiotic metabolism**, centred on two tightly interconnected Reactome pathways: **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** (FDR = 1 × 10⁻⁶, fold-enrichment = 159) and **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (FDR = 1 × 10⁻⁶, fold-enrichment = 122). The overarching **Biological oxidations** pathway (FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 129) captures the widest scope, with 7 of the 9 input metabolites participating.

**Key driver compounds.** Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BaP-DHD-oxide, KEGG C14853) and glutathione (GSH, KEGG C00051) are the two strongest drivers, both annotated to the Phase II conjugation pathway. BaP-DHD-oxide is the ultimate carcinogenic metabolite of benzo[a]pyrene metabolism; it is a classic substrate for glutathione S-transferase (GST)-mediated conjugation, which sequesters it into water-soluble mercapturic acid derivatives for elimination. Glutathione serves as the co-substrate in this conjugation reaction, and both compounds are confirmed members of Reactome pathway R-HSA-156580 ("Phase II – Conjugation of compounds"). β-Mercaptoethanol (C00928) and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) are also matched to this same pathway, consistent with their roles as sulphur-containing or electrophilic intermediates in xenobiotic detoxification.

**Phase I oxidation.** Bromide (C01324), coumarin (C05851) and methimazole (C07190) are assigned to the Phase I functionalization pathway (R-HSA-211945), reflecting their known roles as substrates or inhibitors of cytochrome P450 enzymes. Methimazole, an anti-thyroid drug, is a direct inhibitor of peroxidase-mediated oxidation reactions.

**Biological significance.** The co-enrichment of Phase I and Phase II pathways suggests that the treatment triggers a coordinated xenobiotic-metabolising response, possibly involving induction of CYP450-mediated oxidation followed by glutathione-dependent conjugation. Pantothenic acid (C00864), a cofactor for co-enzyme A biosynthesis, and phosphoserine (C01005), an intermediate in serine biosynthesis, provide ancillary metabolic context but are not primary drivers of the xenobiotic response. The presence of β-mercaptoethanol alongside reduced glutathione is consistent with heightened demand for reduced sulphur pools to fuel conjugation under conditions of electrophilic stress.

**Verified directional relationship.** Both BaP-DHD-oxide (C14853) and glutathione (C00051) are confirmed members of the same Phase II conjugation pathway (R-HSA-156580). GSH operates as the conjugating agent downstream of Phase I bioactivation, whereas BaP-DHD-oxide represents the upstream bioactivated electrophile that is the physiological substrate for GST-catalysed GSH conjugation. Their simultaneous differential abundance in this dataset is therefore mechanistically coherent with a xenobiotic stress response in which Phase I activation products are being scavenged by the glutathione system.
